clue.text: Engineers involved in controversy get a bad name

indicators.note: the engineers are involved in, so placed within, the word for controversy

parts.note: a controversy is a dispute
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers caught up in a row find their reputation tarnished.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepute is the state of having lost respect, of being held in low esteem.

clue.text: Most important phone-call — a lot may hang on it

definitions.text: a lot may hang on it

parts.note: key means crucial, most important
to give someone a ring is to phone them

explanation.surface: A vital phone call on which much depends.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring for holding keys, from which many keys may dangle.

clue.text: Passes some fish as a goodwill gesture

parts.note: to pass something to someone is to hand it, so passes means hands
hake is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Someone hands over fish as a friendly offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking hands is a sign of friendship or agreement.

clue.text: Trim figure without fruit?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the figure word sits around the fruit word

parts.note: a figure is a shape
hips are the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A slim figure that comes from going without fruit?
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means neat and in good order, as on a well-kept vessel.

clue.text: Time is the main issue

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: The question of timing is the key matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like 'the chief' but is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, a stretch of time.

clue.text: Standard names incorrectly applied to cheese

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: the letters of names are set out incorrectly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Standard labels wrongly stuck on a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian grating cheese from the Parma region.

clue.text: An overbold fellow, Percy!

definitions.meaning: Sir Henry Percy, the rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1, had this nickname

explanation.surface: A man named Percy is called reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a headstrong person, and was the nickname of the impetuous medieval nobleman Henry Percy.

clue.text: Allow in the head's painting equipment

indicators.note: the word for allow goes in the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Letting the headmaster's art kit be used.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist mixes colours on a flat board held in the hand.

clue.text: Giving it time, the heartless repeat

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the word the loses its middle letter, its heart, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Give it time and the cruel will do it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again.

clue.text: Exceptionally bitter outside left apt to snap

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the letter for left
the letters of bitter are treated exceptionally, so put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A bitter player on the left wing who is prone to snapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' turns BITTER into BRITTE, which goes 'outside' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle is hard but fragile, and breaks easily.

clue.text: Note brightly coloured and very large screen in the church

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
red is a bright colour
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Notice the bright, huge screen inside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental panel or partition behind an altar.

clue.text: The man working his fingers to the bone?

definitions.text: The man working his fingers to the bone?

parts.words: The man working his fingers to the bone
parts.note: the idiom for toiling hard is read literally: a practitioner whose fingers press on and manipulate bones

explanation.surface: A man who toils tirelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist who treats the body by manipulating the skeleton and muscles.

clue.text: Cut out design drawer — quietly replaced by a good man

indicators.note: the letter for quietly is swapped out and the good man's letters put in its place

parts.note: a drawer is something that draws, such as a pencil
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
ST, short for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A designer's tool is quietly swapped for a worthy fellow's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests furniture but is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a sheet with a pattern cut into it, used to paint the shapes onto a surface.

clue.text: Swan song showing taste

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A swan song that reveals the singer's preferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan song' is a phrase for a final act, but the words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness for something.

clue.text: A new bride needed a place to sleep

indicators.note: new letters are made from bride, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly married woman needed somewhere to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress used for sleeping on, such as when camping.

clue.text: One racing off in all innocence

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry here, so the letters of one and racing are muddled

explanation.surface: A runner leaves the race quite innocently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of ONE plus RACING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is lack of knowledge, and innocence can mean being unaware of wrong.

clue.text: Newsman at the heart of the action may appear dispirited

indicators.note: the newsman word sits at the heart of, inside, the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A reporter at the centre of events might look downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed means low in spirits, unhappy.

clue.text: Making complaint, even with the governor around

indicators.note: the governor word goes around the word for even

parts.note: a king governs, so is a governor
e'en is a poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Moaning about matters, even with the governor present.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is the poetic form of 'even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keening is wailing in lament, a mournful complaint.

clue.text: These days being in flight can be an exciting adventure

indicators.note: the word for these days is being in, placed inside, the word for flight

parts.note: flight means running away, an escape
AD, anno domini, means in the present era

explanation.surface: Being on the run these days can be quite thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit.

clue.text: Gets off the mark

parts.note: the sporting phrase for starting to score is read literally as removing a mark

explanation.definitionFit: Rubs out or wipes away, removing written marks.

clue.text: It's getting awfully late-run the car

indicators.note: the letters of late-run are put together awfully, so jumbled

explanation.surface: It's very late, so run the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Renault is a French car maker and the name of its vehicles.

clue.text: Swearing to give voice about rubbishy stuff

indicators.note: the singing word goes about, around, the rubbish word

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
tat is cheap junk

explanation.surface: Cursing while singing about junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swearing' reads as cursing, but means declaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing as in declaring or affirming something, asserting it.

clue.text: Layer pastry turnover and put the whole lot outside

indicators.note: the whole lot word goes outside the turned pastry

parts.note: a sum is the total, the whole lot

indicators.note: turnover means the pastry word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Stack up a pastry turnover and wrap all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' is a pastry in the surface, but it reverses TART into TRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a bed or band of rock or other material.

clue.text: Foreign dealer who is mean with little hesitation

parts.note: to import is to mean or signify
er is a brief hesitation

explanation.surface: An overseas merchant who is stingy with brief pauses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as stingy but means signify.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer buys goods from abroad to sell at home.

clue.text: Order: make them do wrong!

indicators.note: them do is put together wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to make them misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals an anagram of THEM DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Method means orderly arrangement or system.

clue.text: A Parisienne has got a list, so can't be taken in!

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a, as a Parisian woman would say
a table is a list of data

explanation.surface: A woman from Paris has a list of things she cannot eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneatable food is not fit to be eaten.

clue.text: Plenty to drink?

parts.note: bags is slang for plenty, so bags of a hot drink

explanation.definitionFit: Little sachets of leaves for brewing a cuppa.

clue.text: Chairs not quite enough to seat everyone?

definitions.text: Chairs not quite enough to seat everyone?

parts.words: Chairs not quite enough to seat everyone
parts.note: describes the party game where one seat fewer than the players is set out each round

explanation.surface: A shortage of seating.
explanation.definitionFit: The party game played to music has one seat too few, so a player is out each round.

clue.text: Officer commanding hundreds in the light to stop up

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

indicators.note: the hundreds letter goes in the word for light

parts.note: a clue is a light, something that illuminates a problem
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so a number of hundreds

explanation.surface: An officer commanding hundreds in the light must block the way.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the Roman numeral 500, i.e. hundreds; a clue throws light on a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or close an opening.

clue.text: Looked around food sent back — shocked

indicators.note: the looking word goes around the reversed food

parts.note: stared means looked hard

indicators.note: the food is sent back, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: an egg is a food

explanation.surface: Someone peered at the meal that was returned and was appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered means astonished or deeply surprised.
